judged_text: createAllCalendarEvents runs the create-on-every-matching-credential fan-out once per credential-less destination, so an array holding two legacy (NULL credentialId) destination calendars of the same integration executes the fan-out twice. A COLLECTIVE booking whose two hosts both have legacy destination calendar rows gets the same event created twice on every matching credential - duplicate calendar events on each host - and each duplicate yields its own BookingReference row; review-base ran this fan-out exactly once for the single destination.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the new logic iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and, for each destination with no `credentialId`, executes a fan-out across *all* matching credentials (`this.calendarCredentials.filter((c) => c.type === destination.integration)` then `map(...createEvent(c, event))`). If `event.destinationCalendar` contains multiple legacy destinations (NULL `credentialId`) of the same `integration` (plausible now that `destinationCalendar` is an array and COLLECTIVE pushes multiple hosts' destination calendars in `handleNewBooking`), this fan-out will run once per such destination, creating duplicate events per credential. This matches the finding and is directly implied by the diff.
